entities.summary: Alessandro Mattei was an Italian Cardinal and a significant figure in papal diplomacy of the Napoleonic period, playing a crucial role in the diplomatic efforts of Pope Pius VII to maintain the independence of the Papal States from Napoleon's France. Mattei's diplomatic skills and experience as a member of the Roman aristocratic House of Mattei made him a key advisor to the Pope, and he successfully negotiated several important treaties and agreements with French officials, including the Treaty of Fontainebleau in 1814. Through his efforts, Mattei helped to secure the temporary status of the Papal States as a sovereign entity, despite the eventual loss of their independence in 1870. The legacy of Alessandro Mattei's diplomatic work can be seen in the continued importance of the Papal States as a symbol of Catholicism and the enduring role of the Catholic Church in Italian politics. The diplomatic skills and experience of Alessandro Mattei have also been studied by historians as an important example of the role of the papacy in European diplomacy during the Napoleonic era.
